title: Station Zen: Calm Metro Builder
audience: Relaxation seekers, new-to-genre players, commuters and cozy-puzzle fans aged 10+, plus transit and map enthusiasts. Players put off by the stress, harsh sudden failure and thin onboarding of existing metro-routing games.
controls:
<![CDATA[All controls are touch, and one finger is enough.
- Drag from a station end to extend a line. Drag from a station to an empty station to start a line (needs a free line).
- Drag a line end to a new station to redraw. Drag a mid-segment to bend it through a new station, or drag the line off the map to a bin zone to delete it. Releasing it back where it started cancels the edit.
- Tap a station to see its demand card and queue count. Tap a train to see its load.
- Hold anywhere for 0.3s to pause and plan, and release to resume. Double-tap the pause chip to lock the pause.
- Two-finger pinch and pan to zoom and move the map. This is free from the start and the tutorial never locks it.
- Undo and redo buttons sit in a thumb-reach bottom bar. A 1x/2x/3x fast-forward button sits beside them.
- Weekly card: tap to pick one, with a long-press to preview its effect on the map.
- Accessibility: colour-blind patterns (dashed, dotted, double, wavy line styles plus a shape badge on each line), large-touch mode, reduce-motion, haptics on/off, one-handed layout flip for left or right hand, text size, and high contrast.
- Skip is always visible on the tutorial, and all cutscenes can be skipped.]]>
core_loop:
<![CDATA[30-second loop: stations appear on the map, passengers show a glyph (circle, triangle, square, and so on) for where they want to go. The player drags from a station to draw or extend a line, or drags a line end to redraw it. Trains carry passengers and the player watches the network flow. A soft overcrowd ring around a station fills as passengers pile up, and the player reroutes.
Session loop (5-10 min): each in-game week brings new stations and a pick-one card (new line, train, carriage, tunnel, interchange, or a calm card). The player adapts the network. The run ends at a gentle failure, or when the star goals are met. A Heatmap Replay then shows where the network strained, with one suggestion tip.
Meta loop: stars unlock cities, and city mastery unlocks line and train skins and a Station Garden diorama. Daily puzzle and streaks bring players back. Weekly rotating Ghost Rivals add competition.
Calm design pillars:
- Pause-and-plan is free and unlimited. Hold anywhere to freeze time, and drawing while frozen is allowed.
- Undo is available for the last 3 edits, and also during a pause.
- Overcrowding is never a surprise. It escalates through a soft yellow glow, an amber pulse and a gentle chime, then a 'Last Call' that gives the player time to act and offers a Breather (below). A run ends only after the ring has stayed full for a long grace window.
- A run can be saved and resumed at any time, with no punishment for leaving.]]>

positioning: The gentlest metro builder on the store: pause anytime, undo anything, never a surprise game over. A calm, accessible way into the transit-routing genre, with warm generative audio, a cosy Station Garden collection and fair, friendly online play. 'Plan it slowly. Watch it flow.'
progression:
<![CDATA[Player-facing meta:
- Stars unlock cities (10), and each city has a Mastery track (stars, endless score tiers, daily completion) with 5 tiers. Each tier unlocks line colour skins, train skins (steam, tram, bullet and so on) and Station Garden diorama pieces.
- Station Garden: a cozy diorama of the player's favourite city, decorated with collected items (benches, lanterns, trees, tiny passengers). It is visible on the profile and shareable as a postcard image.
- Passenger Journal: a collection of small passenger characters, each with a short story card unlocked by serving specific glyph pairs.
- Daily Puzzle with a 7-day streak ribbon (with 1 free streak freeze per week, earnable). Weekly Ghost Rivals: a seeded run where the player's score is compared against generated-name ghost scores (async, level-matched ±2 tiers via a rating). Friend rooms by code share a seed and compare scores, with a fixed set of emotes only.
- Online leaderboards per city and per Daily, and quick-match Duel Mode: two players solve the same seed side by side and compare passengers delivered, calm to read, with an AI opponent fallback after 20 seconds without a match. Disconnect before start has no penalty, and results are server-authoritative.
- Level-ups of the player (Commuter Rank 1-50) give soft currency (Tokens), boosters and cosmetic items.
- Return reasons: daily puzzle, streak, weekly ghost, seasonal city themes (cherry blossom, snow) in a free track pass, Station Garden completion and the Journal.]]>

level_structure:
<![CDATA[Structure: 10 cities (chapters), each a handcrafted fictional city, 12-14 levels each, for 130 campaign levels. There is also an Endless mode per city and a Daily Puzzle (seeded).
A level is a timed in-game scenario of 6-12 in-game weeks (2-8 real minutes) with a fixed starting map, a scripted station spawn order (handcrafted, with light randomised variation of glyph mix) and fixed resources. Each level has an 'aha' (a specific insight). Star goals per level:
- 1 star: survive to the target week.
- 2 stars: deliver N passengers.
- 3 stars: a special goal, such as 'no station above amber', 'use only 2 lines', 'finish with a loop line'. Stars are earned in any order and kept permanently.
Pacing per city: levels 1-3 teach or twist the new rule, 4-6 combine it with earlier ones, 7 is a breather (relaxed spawn rate, decorative goal), 8-10 raise tension, 11 is a spike/mini-boss ('Rush Hour Festival'), 12 is a gentle Mastery level, and 13-14 are optional bonus 'Postcard' puzzle levels with fixed layouts.
Cities (chapters), each with one new rule or mechanic:
1. Willowmere (tutorial village): lines, glyph demand, pause-and-plan, undo. 12 levels (the first 4 are guided, skippable in under 90s total).
2. Portside Bay: river and tunnels.
3. Kitebrook: trains and carriages, load limits.
4. Amberhill: hills, slow-gradient segments. Express trains skip stations.
5. Lotus Delta: islands and ferry links.
6. Frostholm: weather (snow slows trains, with a calm palette shift).
7. Sunbazaar: interchanges and transfer hubs, and a market event that spikes demand.
8. Ringvale: ring-shaped city with a loop line, where one-way tracks are introduced.
9. Neon Quay: night city, with rush-hour waves and demand forecasts.
10. Grand Meridian (finale): all mechanics combined. Mastery levels.
Level count: Willowmere 12, Portside 13, Kitebrook 13, Amberhill 13, Lotus 13, Frostholm 13, Sunbazaar 13, Ringvale 13, Neon Quay 13, Grand Meridian 14 = 130 levels.
Per-city unlock: 60% of the previous city's stars, or a free 'Day Pass' alternative from daily play. Nothing is gated behind payment.
Full roster of mechanics/obstacles/boosters (12):
1. Lines (colour plus pattern). 2. Glyph demand. 3. River tunnels. 4. Carriages. 5. Interchanges. 6. Express trains. 7. Ferry links. 8. Weather slowdowns. 9. One-way tracks. 10. Demand forecast (peek at the next 2 stations). 11. Rush-hour waves. 12. Heritage stations (protected, cannot be rerouted, and give bonus stars).
Boosters (all earnable free, no cash-only items): Breather (clears overcrowd and gives 20s of calm), Rewind (undo the last in-game day), Peek (show the next 3 stations), Express Pass (a free temporary train), Hold the Clock (extends the pause for a heavy plan phase). Boosters are capped at 2 per level.]]>
difficulty_curve:
<![CDATA[Sawtooth with gentle spikes. Target first-attempt win rate: Willowmere ~95%, then falling to ~70% in the Grand Meridian finale, with unlimited retries and no lives.
- Levels 1-12 (Willowmere): ramp 0.05 to 0.3, fully guided, no failures possible in the first 3 levels.
- Each city: 3 teaching levels at the previous level's difficulty minus 0.05 (a breather), then +0.05 per level until the spike (level 11) at about +0.12, followed by an easy Mastery level.
- Spikes at levels 11 of each city (the Rush Hour Festival); breathers at level 7 of each city and at every city's first level.
- Failure is soft: after an overcrowd, the run offers 'Try again from week X' (checkpoint every 3 weeks), 'Use Breather', or 'Keep going with a new plan' using a wide grace window. Dynamic assist: after 3 failures on a level, offer (opt-in) a +1 free line or longer grace. Stars are never reduced by assist, and a small 'Assisted' badge is shown, but all rewards are the same.
- Endless and Daily difficulty scale slowly, with a 'calm' mode that stops spawns at a set pace for pure relaxation.]]>
camera_orientation: Portrait by default, one-handed. The map is a fixed, zoomable 2D top-down diagram with free pinch-zoom and pan from the first second. Landscape is supported on tablets, with a simple layout change only.
market_opportunity: <![CDATA[Demand for minimalist transit-routing puzzles is large, and reviews of the leaders consistently cite stress, missing undo, thin onboarding, harsh sudden failure, thin meta and few accessibility options. This game answers each gap directly. Search demand is high for 'metro game' and 'relaxing puzzle game' (broad 'strategy games' is dominated by big RTS apps, so ASO targets the long-tail calm/relaxing/metro terms, not the broad head term). Casual cosy players are a big audience on both stores, with low competition for a polished calm entry. Key risk: keyword winnability is low for broad terms, so the plan relies on store creative (calm screenshots, 'No stress' angle), the long tails, and the viral postcard share. Distinct glyph set and UI are needed to stay clear of the reference game.]]>
competitor_contrast:
<![CDATA[Versus the leading minimalist metro puzzle: a pause-and-plan mode with unlimited free freeze, undo/redo, soft escalating overcrowd warnings with a grace window instead of a sudden failure, a guided but skippable under-90s tutorial, 130 handcrafted levels in 10 themed cities with star goals, colour-blind line patterns, a Heatmap Replay with tips, a collectible Station Garden and Passenger Journal, daily puzzles, and fair online duels. Visual identity is warm paper-craft, rounded glyph set (leaf, drop, kite, lantern, moon, key, cup, star) and a pastel palette, not the reference's flat geometric glyphs and white background. No subscriptions, no pay-to-win.
Versus the strategy-war apps named in the player research (AoW3, Boom Beach): no pay-to-win, no timers, no subscriptions, fair matchmaking with bot fallback, no forced tutorial.]]>
economy_monetization:
<![CDATA[Principle: trust. Spending buys cosmetics and convenience, never power or access. No lives, no timers, no energy, no subscriptions, no gacha, no loot boxes.
Soft currency: Tokens (earned from stars, daily, ghost rivals, Commuter Rank). Used to buy boosters, skins and garden items. No paid-only boosters.
Premium currency: none. IAP is direct purchase of items.
IAP (all one-time and permanent):
- Remove Ads ($3.99): removes interstitials and banner-like prompts, and also gives free rewarded-ad boosters.
- Supporter Pack ($4.99): a set of skins and garden items, and 3 extra Undo slots (undo depth 3 to 6). This is a QoL option and is also earnable with Tokens.
- Cosmetic bundles ($1.99 to $6.99): line skins, train skins, garden themes, tune packs (audio themes), city-themed postcards.
- Starter Pack ($0.99): a skin plus 10 booster uses.
- Free-track Season Pass with an optional premium cosmetic track ($4.99) that is capped, never required, and never grants power. Each season cycle is about 8 weeks.
- Total core QoL bundle cap about $10. The Complete Collector bundle is cosmetic only.
Ads:
- Rewarded video, opt-in only, to get a booster, a double-token claim, or a retry checkpoint. The reward always grants even if the ad fails or hangs, and the close button appears within 5 seconds (hard cap).
- Interstitials: only between levels, at most once every 3 completed levels and with a 4-minute minimum gap. Never in the first session, never during a run or a pause, and never after a failure. Removed by Remove Ads.
- No dark patterns: no spend-triggered difficulty change, matchmaking uses only rating and seed, and Duel/Ghost rating inputs are transparent in a help sheet. Online fairness: matches are within ±2 rating tiers in at least 90% of cases, with an AI/ghost fallback after 20-30 seconds.
- Cloud save: cross-platform account via email code or platform sign-in (resend within 60s), with a restore-purchases flow and a no-wipe guarantee. Purchased and earned items are never nerfed or removed. Changes are compensated.
- Revenue levers: ad-removal conversion, cosmetic bundles, season pass cosmetics, and rewarded booster use. Target: ARPDAU of about $0.05-0.09, with ad-free players converting at about 3%.]]>
technical_assumptions: React Native with Skia for map rendering and Reanimated worklets for gestures and animation; 60fps on mid-range Android and 4GB RAM devices
Deterministic seeded simulation (fixed timestep) shared by client and server so Daily, Ghost and Duel results are server-verifiable and replayable

Server-authoritative results for online modes; disconnect before match start cancels with no penalty after 20s; crash or sync-error results are auto-refunded and the replay is shown on the result screen
Matchmaking by rating tier (±2 in at least 90% of matches), AI/ghost fallback after 20-30s; every online mode works against AI
Local-first save with cloud sync; checkpoint every 3 in-game weeks; resume after app kill
Generative audio via pre-rendered stem layers triggered by game events, with a small bundle size; app download under 150MB, lazy-loaded city assets
Online uses generated names and a fixed emote set only, with no chat or typed text; a report button for abuse
Cross-platform account (email code or platform sign-in), restore purchases, no-wipe policy
Haptics through the platform API and a colour-blind-safe palette with a pattern overlay verified by a simulator
Offline play for all campaign, endless and daily modes; online only for duels, ghosts, rooms and leaderboards
Live-ops via remote config (season themes, daily seeds); no mandatory new meta-systems without a skip and an on/off switch
Interstitials and rewarded ads through a standard mediation SDK with a 5s close guarantee and reward-on-hang fallback
qa_acceptance_criteria: First-session tutorial can be skipped at any point and completes in under 90s when played; pinch-zoom and pan work from the first frame
Hold-to-pause freezes simulation instantly (<100ms) and drawing/editing works while frozen; undo/redo restore the last 3 edits exactly
Overcrowd escalates through yellow, amber and Last Call stages and never ends a run before the full grace window elapses; no sudden game over
All 130 campaign levels are completable, with 1/2/3-star goals verified by bot playtests; difficulty and win-rate targets are met within tolerance
Each mechanic (tunnels, carriages, interchanges, express, ferries, weather, one-way, forecast, rush waves, heritage) is introduced in its chapter with a teaching level
Colour-blind line patterns and shape badges are distinguishable under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulation

Rewarded ads always grant the reward, even on hang or failure; close button appears within 5s; no interstitial in the first session, during a run, pause or after a failure; interstitials are capped at 1 per 3 levels with a 4-minute gap
All purchases are permanent and restorable; no content or boosters are cash-only; no item or progress is nerfed or removed without compensation

Online: matches are within ±2 rating tiers in at least 90% of cases; the bot/ghost fallback starts within 30s; disconnect before match start is never a loss; crash/sync losses are auto-refunded and the result and replay show on the same screen
Online supports a fixed set of emotes only, with no chat or typed text and generated names; a report button works
Cloud save and restore work across devices; email code resend within 60s; resume after app kill returns to the last checkpoint
Sustains 60fps on a 4GB mid-range Android with 40+ stations on screen; install size under 150MB; no crashes in a 30-minute soak
Heatmap Replay renders for every finished run and shows the top 3 strain hotspots with a tip
Daily Puzzle is identical for all players, streak freeze works, and the date rollover handles time zones
Content rating is Everyone with no violence, gambling, loot boxes or chat; all analytics events fire with correct params
store_listing_strategy: Title: 'Station Zen: Calm Metro Builder'. Short description: 'Draw metro lines. Pause anytime. Undo anything. No stress.' Keyword focus on long-tail terms: 'relaxing metro game', 'calm puzzle game', 'metro builder', 'train line puzzle', 'zen puzzle', with 'strategy games' as a secondary term only (the head term is not winnable). Screenshots lead with the calm pillars (pause-and-plan, undo, soft warnings), then the 10 cities, the Station Garden and the accessibility options. A 15s preview video shows a satisfying line draw with generative music. Ask for ratings after a 3-star win, never after a failure. Use the shareable postcard for organic growth. Soft-launch in India, Southeast Asia and Latin America to tune retention, then go global.
